headline: High: ms-swift can write and execute code against shared files, while spring-integration-samples has no isolation or runtime protections documented, creating default-pathway risks of prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can read/write files and run shell/Python, and agent_b has no documented isolation or provenance controls. A shared workspace or manual handoff would let attacker-controlled content from ms-swift influence spring-integration-samples, but the pair does not document a default bridge, so this is not high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or copied files are passed from agent_a to agent_b, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF agent_b parses file contents as instructions, attacker-controlled text from agent_a can steer behavior.
mitigations: Separate working directories for each agent.
Disable automatic ingestion of files produced by the other agent.
Add a manual review step before any cross-agent handoff.
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to all inter-agent files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches secrets-like artifacts such as hub_token and sdk-token and can read/write files, while agent_b has network_egress none and no data classes or file surfaces documented. Leakage is possible only if data is manually transferred or a shared workspace exists; the blast radius appears limited by agent_b's lack of egress.
conditions: IF agent_a writes secrets or sensitive outputs into a shared folder, agent_b can read them from disk.
IF operator copies sensitive logs from agent_a into agent_b inputs, those contents may be exposed in agent_b outputs.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared directories.
Rotate any token exposed in agent_a logs.
Use separate OS users for each agent.
Restrict agent_b inputs to sanitized summaries.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace ACLs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has filesystem write and shell execution, but agent_b exposes no write, network, or mutable-resource capabilities in its profile. There is no documented overlapping write surface, so direct conflict is unlikely; uncertainty stays low because agent_b's runtime surface is sparse and unverified.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF agent_b is wrapped in an external orchestrator that adds hidden write scopes, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to shared files.
Serialize any handoff through a queue.
Check for hidden wrapper permissions before launch.
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate files, logs, and training outputs that agent_b could consume if the operator wires them together, and agent_b has no documented verification step or critical-evaluation behavior. The pair lacks a default safe handoff, so A's outputs may be treated as authoritative by B in common workflows.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a's generated files or stdout without validation, errors can cascade.
IF agent_a emits incorrect facts into a downstream workflow, agent_b may propagate them into travel-planning outputs.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents.
Require source citations for any factual claims.
Compare outputs against an independent check.
Limit agent_b to drafting, not acting.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoff payloads.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a handles hub_token and sdk-token and may process datasets, models, checkpoints, and logs, while agent_b has no documented data residency, retention, or certification constraints. A compliance mismatch is plausible only if regulated data is routed through agent_a into agent_b, but the profiles do not show such a default flow.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed by agent_a and then exported into agent_b workflows, residency or retention obligations may be violated.
IF agent_a logs sensitive artifacts into files retained by a shared operator, compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Review retention settings on agent_a logs.
Avoid storing secrets in training outputs.
Document data flow before deployment.
requires-engineering: map residency and retention controls end-to-end.
